study: Nyhan & Reifler (2015), Displacing Misinformation about Events: An Experimental Test of Causal Corrections, Journal of Experimental Political Science
data_source: OSF FLoRA reproduction node 5vx27 (author materials + rebuilt data). Data: component 'Data' (2e9xr) file causal-replication.dta (guid 86zqr), N=1000 raw / 764-987 analytical. Code: nyhan-reifler-causal-corrections.do (guid km2vb). Human-flora reproduction log: PushButtonReproduction.smcl (guid 2czmp). Paper itself is closed-access (no OA full text); headline numbers were taken from the bushel-trace claim file (u3nw4), the PBR_ADR audit template, and the Transparency Trail docx.

blw3kn / Model 1 (swensenfav, aweight).paper: denial vs control -0.39 p<0.01; causal vs innuendo 0.66 p<0.01

m638d7 / Model 2 (swensenfav, survey).paper: denial vs control -0.41 p<0.01; causal vs innuendo 0.32 p<0.05

key_findings: All six Table 2 OLS models were independently re-computed from causal-replication.dta (WLS with the 'aw' analytic weight and, for the survey columns, pweight='weight'). Coefficient point estimates match the shared Stata reproduction log (PushButtonReproduction.smcl) and the paper's reported values to the decimal place.

All six bushel-trace contrast claims verified exactly: -0.39, -0.41, -0.48, -0.36, -0.34, -0.16 (Models 1-6); the focal Model 5 main claim (denial -0.25 SE0.07, causal -0.58 SE0.07, diff -0.34 p<0.01) also reproduced.
Statistical significance thresholds in the paper hold in the recomputation (Model 2 causal-vs-innuendo p=0.044<0.05; Model 4 p=0.012<0.05; Model 6 p=0.112 reported as <0.12).

Survey-design (svy) standard errors were approximated with WLS + HC1 robust errors; point estimates are identical to Stata's svy output, SEs agree to ~3 decimals (not byte-identical to Stata's linearized variance).
No contradicted or failed headline claim.
how_verified: Reran provided Stata do-file logic in Python (statsmodels WLS) and cross-checked in R (statsmodels/lm). All recomputed coefficients equal the human FLoRA Stata log exactly.
notes: Minor documentation gap (P2): the do-file's svy: commands rely on a prior svyset (pweight=weight) not declared inside the file, so the survey regressions are not fully self-contained (the smcl log shows them running). Cosmetic (P3): svy SEs reproduced to ~3 decimals rather than bit-exact via HC1 approximation. These do not affect any headline number. No paywalled article PDF was downloaded; all kept materials are OSF/FLoRA open assets.
